Subject: Helix post-demo: model slate calibration, cost bridging & pilot asks

Hi Priya / Sam —

Thanks again for the time today — good discussion and helpful context on your real-time summarization use case and the latency SLOs you care about (sub-350ms p50 on short queries, burst to 200 qps). Per our demo and the test prompts you shared, we sketched a recommended slate and a short rationale for each option below. I’m including benchmark links and the prompt set we used (attached).

Recommended slate (tradeoffs at a glance):
- Redwood-2-8B-quant (preferred) — best cost/latency balance for Helix: p50 ~120–180ms, quantized 4-bit path keeps CPU/GPU memory low. Quality: strong for summarization and instruction-following. Caveat: slightly higher repetition on very long context unless KV cache warmed.
- OpenX-Chat-13B (safety-finetuned) — higher quality on nuanced instructions, p50 ~260–330ms, token cost higher; good fallback for edge-case documents where fidelity matters.
- LlamaFast-4x (low-latency distilled) — fastest p50 ~60–110ms, lower cost, but tradeoff in hallucination risk for the trickier extraction prompts. Good for high-volume near-deterministic transforms.

Attachments / links: benchmark CSV with 1k prompt sample results, and the exact prompt set (helix_prompt_set_v1.json). See Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-Helix-Demo-Assets

Key asks / next steps:
1) Confirm target pilot scope (we proposed 2-week sandbox + 2-week load validation).
2) Confirm which SLA tier you want for the pilot (best-effort vs reserved capacity). Reserved changes cost estimates.
3) We’ll run a focused regression eval on your high-risk prompt subset (we highlighted ~80 prompts in the attached prompt set).

If you’re open, we can put together a tight pilot SOW and an estimated cost bridge showing token spend for the different slates (1M tokens baseline). Karthik — can you add the 1M-token run-rate ballpark for each model and an estimated p50/p95 per model here?

Thanks — feel free to reply to this thread and we’ll route the appropriate data and SOW.

—

Monica — thanks for the clear recap and the benchmark pack. Quick clarifying questions from our side after reading the CSV and trying a couple prompts: 

1) Latency SLO — our product team is strict about p95 for live traffic. Can you call out p95 numbers (not just p50) for the three models on the short-query bucket? We can tolerate a slightly higher p50 but need p95 < 700ms routinely.
2) Data handling — for the pilot, can Redwood guarantee no prompt material will be used to train public models and that logs are isolated per tenant? We need a short paragraph on that for our security/compliance team.
3) Cost — rough per-1M-token delta is useful. Can you give a line-item estimate for the three slates?

Also attaching two additional sample prompts we didn’t include in the demo that trip the hallucination case — would appreciate those in the regression eval.

Hi Priya — quick answers + numbers (ran on our staging cluster using your short-query sample set + the two extra prompts Priya attached):

p50 / p95 (short-query bucket, median of 5 runs):
- Redwood-2-8B-quant: p50 150ms, p95 420ms
- OpenX-Chat-13B: p50 295ms, p95 680ms
- LlamaFast-4x: p50 85ms, p95 240ms

Cost per 1M tokens (approx, hosted pricing for pilot):
- Redwood-2-8B-quant: $210 / 1M tokens
- OpenX-Chat-13B: $410 / 1M tokens
- LlamaFast-4x: $95 / 1M tokens

Notes:
- The p95 for Redwood-2-8B-quant is sensitive to cold KV cache for long conversation threads — warm-up caching for frequent prefixes reduces the p95 by ~120–150ms in our runs.
- OpenX-Chat-13B delivers the best semantic fidelity for edge-case instructions but has the highest cost and tail-latency risk during bursts unless run on reserved capacity.
- LlamaFast-4x is viable where latency/cost matter most, but we recommend an automated fallback to OpenX-Chat-13B for prompts flagged by your hallucination detector.

Proposed pilot eval plan (timeline):
- Week 0: SOW & access + test dataset ingest (2 days)
- Week 1: Parallel A/B runs across 3 models on your sample set (includes 1k high-risk prompts)
- Week 2: Load validation and p95 stress runs; integrate prefix caching
- Week 3: Quality review and decision meeting; produce final recommendation and cost bridge

I’ve attached the prompt set we’ll use (helix_prompt_set_v1.json) and the small script we’ll run to flag hallucination risk. If you confirm scope, Monica will send a pilot SOW draft and the HubSpot/DocuSign links.

—
